summary: Re-verified Nabidka layout fix only (frontend, no backend). Result: FIX DID NOT WORK on desktop ≥1024px. The new CSS (align-self: stretch + min-height: 320px, no height:100%) caused the implicit grid-row to be pinned to exactly 320px because min-height on a single grid child sets the row's minimum size. Result: img stretches to 320px (✅), but .process-content's text overflows its 320px grid cell, making the .process-item bounding box 369–417px. So img is still NOT matching item row height (diff 49–97px > 5px tolerance). Mobile 390x800 stack order img→num→content→detail is correct ✅. DOM JSX order img→num→content→detail correct ✅.

ui_bugs.issue: img still does not stretch to full row height. Measured @1440x900: item 0 row=417px img=320px (diff 97px); items 1-3 row=369-370px img=320px (diff 49-50px). Computed gridTemplateRows='320px' confirms the row itself is pinned at 320px by the img's min-height. .process-content's rect_h is also 320 but its inner text overflows downward (no overflow:hidden), pushing .process-item's measured height to 417px while the grid row stays 320. align-self:stretch IS being applied (computed alignSelf='stretch') but it stretches img to the (broken) 320px row, not to natural content height.

action_items: REMOVE 'min-height: 320px' from .process-img desktop override at /app/frontend/src/App.css lines 1007-1013. With min-height removed, the grid row will size naturally to the tallest cell (.process-content text), and align-self:stretch will then stretch the image to fill that natural row height.

Alternative if a tall image is desired: set explicit grid-template-rows to a fixed height on .process-item (e.g. 360px) AND add overflow:hidden or min-height:100% on .process-content so text doesn't overflow. Less flexible — first option is cleaner.
After fix, re-run measurement: at 1440x900 each .process-item row height should equal .process-img height within 5px.
critical_code_review_comments: Setting min-height on a single grid child to control row height is a brittle pattern — it can pin the row and cause sibling overflow, exactly what happened here. Prefer letting content size the row and using align-self:stretch on the image.

There is no overflow guard on .process-content; if the grid row is forced shorter than text content, the text bleeds out of the cell silently (no visible scrollbar). Worth adding either overflow handling or asserting natural sizing.

Mobile bleed is intentional: .process-img base style uses width: calc(100% + 48px) with negative margins to bleed image to viewport edges (img_w=390 vs item_w=342). Confirm this is desired UX — measured but not flagged as a bug.

success_rate.frontend: 67% (2 of 3 sub-checks pass: DOM order ✅, mobile stack ✅, desktop full-height ❌)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Only the desktop full-height issue remains. To verify quickly: viewport 1440x900, open /nabidka, evaluate getComputedStyle(.process-item).gridTemplateRows — it should NOT be a fixed '320px'. Each .process-item bounding height should equal its .process-img bounding height within 5px on all 4 items. Mobile stack order and DOM JSX order are already correct.
rca of the issue: Bug: img height (320px) < item row height (369-417px). RCA: in /app/frontend/src/App.css lines 1007-1013, .process-img has min-height:320px. Because .process-img is a grid item, this min-height becomes the grid row's minimum size, so gridTemplateRows resolves to '320px' for all four items. align-self:stretch then correctly stretches img to fill that 320px row, but .process-content's text content is taller than 320px and overflows visually outside its grid cell, making the .process-item element bounding box 369-417px. The image is NOT short — the GRID ROW itself is too short, and the image dutifully matches it. Mitigation: drop min-height:320px (or lower it well below natural content height) so the row sizes to the tallest item naturally; align-self:stretch then auto-fits the image to that row.
